title: Mark (25 April)
hookLine: the evangelist behind the Gospel that starts with a voice in the desert; his symbol is the lion

cards: No manger. No angels. No family tree.
One sentence of title, and then a shout from the wilderness. That's how the Gospel of Mark begins, in the Douay-Rheims: "The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God."
A few lines later, a voice crying in the desert, John the Baptist in camel's hair, and Jesus already walking down to the river. Some readers call it the Gospel in a hurry.
So who was its writer, and why is his sign a lion?

teach.h: THE GOSPEL NEVER NAMES ITS WRITER.
teach.b: The Gospel itself never says who Mark was. Tradition fills in the name.
An early bishop, Papias, wrote that Mark had been Peter's interpreter, and set down what Peter remembered of the Lord's words and deeds.

Tradition also links him with the John Mark of the Acts of the Apostles, whose mother's house in Jerusalem was a place where the believers gathered, and who set out with Paul and Barnabas, then turned back partway.
Paul refused to take him on the next journey, and Paul and Barnabas split over it. Yet in a later letter Paul asks for Mark to be brought to him, because he is useful.

teach.h: JOHN MARK: FAILED ONCE, TRUSTED AGAIN.
teach.b: A young man who failed once, and was trusted again. Some readers even wonder whether the young man in Mark's Gospel who runs off naked from Gethsemane when Jesus is arrested is the writer quietly signing his work.
Nobody can know. Now the lion. Christians long ago matched the four Gospel writers with the four living creatures in Ezekiel and Revelation: a man, a lion, an ox and an eagle.

teach.h: A LION FOR A ROARING VOICE.
teach.b: Saint Jerome gave Mark the lion, because his Gospel opens with a voice roaring in the wilderness: "A voice of one crying in the desert: Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make straight his paths."

teach.h: PREPARE YE THE WAY OF THE LORD.
teach.b: Venice later took Mark as its patron, and his winged lion still stands over the city. A short Gospel, a loud beginning, and a writer who was given a second chance.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Mark the Evangelist on 25 April, reading from his Gospel at Mass; in Venice, where tradition says his relics rest, his day is a great civic and church feast.

games.q: you're Paul. John Mark turned back partway on your last journey. now Barnabas wants to bring him again. what do you do?
o: refuse, even if it costs you Barnabas.
games.why: Paul refused, and he and Barnabas went separate ways. later Paul wrote asking for Mark, because he was useful.

practice: Open a Bible or an app to Mark, chapter one, a short read, or just picture how it opens, with a voice in the desert.

Notice the pace: Jesus is always on the move, the river, the desert, the lake, a house full of people, a lonely place before dawn. If you pray, ask to hear it as if for the first time; if you don't, simply take it as a story.

wordCard.voice: Mark. The evangelist the Church names as writer of the Gospel that opens with a voice in the desert, marked by the lion.

orig.note: Greek: Mark's name as the New Testament writes it.
